data.title: bn-2lir: name and fix the rocks LOCK EWOULDBLOCK mechanism
data.description: Mechanism named with measurement, not argument. ident::Id::new() is (31.25ms bucket shifted left 64) OR fastrand::u128 low 64 bits; fastrand 2.5.0 seeds its thread-local RNG from DefaultHasher::new() (SipHash-1-3 with FIXED all-zero keys, NOT RandomState) over just Instant::now() plus ThreadId (global_rng.rs:31,203-213). In a freshly exec'd nextest child the ThreadId is constant, so the whole 64-bit random half is a pure function of one CLOCK_MONOTONIC nanosecond. Two processes reading the same nanosecond mint the byte-identical Id and therefore the byte-identical /tmp path. Measured: 14 dup Ids per 400k burst-spawned processes (every dup Id carried a dup fastrand::get_seed), and 2 collisions in 4000 bursts of 29 simultaneous processes (29 = tests here that mint a DB), so about 5e-4 per suite run, not 2^-64. Lock-type finding: rocksdb 8.1.1 uses fcntl F_SETLK F_WRLCK (env/fs_posix.cc:95-106) and reports EAGAIN as 'While lock file: X: Resource temporarily unavailable' (fs_posix.cc:785-786). POSIX record locks are per-(process,inode) and never self-conflict; RocksDB's same-process guard is a path-keyed locked_files map that returns a DIFFERENT error (ENOLCK, 'lock hold by current process', fs_posix.cc:761-773). So the observed message proves a cross-process conflict, which kills bone candidates 1/3/4 as explanations and confirms the cross-process path collision. Candidate 2 also dead: drop closes the handle before touching the dir. Fix: tmp_db_path() names dirs mess_db-PID-SEQ-Id and creates them with exclusive create_dir. Uniqueness is structural (no two live processes share a pid, no two calls share a seq). No sleep, no retry. svc::test_actor::TmpHandle shared the same unsafe naming and now shares the helper. Instrumentation also landed: tmp_db_report() prints path, pid, thread, dir contents, open-fd count and this pid's live tmp dirs on any failure; drop no longer unwraps DB::destroy (panic-in-drop during unwind aborts and loses the real failure). Regression tests pin both halves; negative control with the old naming fails with two identical /tmp/333rrg-36yctttg-tfxq5d paths. Bounded repro: 200 foreground iterations of rocks+svc against unfixed trunk, 0 failures - the expected outcome at 5e-4/run, reported as a weak negative. Evidence: mess_db 46/46 pass, full suite 1196/1196 pass, cargo check --workspace --all-targets clean, clippy -p mess_db clean, just fmt-check clean.
